edges.effect_quant: The clearest older placebo-controlled IBS trial found satisfactory global response in 82% of ispaghula users versus 53% with placebo, while constipation and transit time improved significantly. Later fiber reviews suggest the effect is real but mainly bowel-habit focused rather than dramatic symptom reversal.
edges.population: adults with constipation-predominant irritable bowel syndrome or IBS with constipation-heavy bowel symptoms
edges.mechanism: Psyllium increases stool water and bulk while preserving softness better than many insoluble fibers, which can improve transit and bowel regularity in IBS-C without the same tendency to worsen irritation as coarse bran.
edges.summary: Psyllium husk is one of the few fiber interventions that remains reasonably defensible in IBS-C. The benefit is usually strongest for bowel habit and overall satisfaction, while pain and bloating relief are less consistent than the marketing often suggests.
edges.caveats: This is not a complete IBS fix, and soluble fiber can still aggravate bloating in some people. The literature supports psyllium more for constipation-dominant presentations than for mixed or diarrhea-predominant IBS.
